scope: read-only contract audit, no new probe/code/runtime/device/security action
question: Do SDK identity or native HAL binding contracts establish why retained per-IOProc masks still yielded nonnull disabled-direction buffers?

findings.claim: A created AudioDeviceIOProcID identifies a callback registration together with its clientdata and is permitted wherever a regular IOProc is used; same callback may be registered repeatedly with different contexts.
findings.consequence: The opaque returned ID is not semantically replaced by the raw original callback address.

findings.claim: The frozen helper registers process with two distinct Context pointers, requires distinct returned IDs, copies each returned ID into mIOProc, and configures one stream of each direction separately.
findings.consequence: No contract evidence justifies substituting raw process function pointers or merging the registrations.

findings.claim: Per-IOProc stream usage is selected by registration and direction, covers all streams in that direction, and unused streams are specified to deliver null callbackdata while retaining byte size.
findings.consequence: Keep the NULL assertion; successful mask readback plus nonnull callback remains an unresolved discrepancy.

findings.claim: AudioServerPlugIn client IDs are UInt32 host-provided client identities, distinct from PID and capable of distinguishing multiple clients in one process. The admitted contracts do not define a one-to-one mapping from application IOProcID to plug-in clientID.
findings.consequence: Do not equate an IOProc pointer or PID with the native client counter identifier.

findings.claim: Native StartIO tracks active device-client IDs, starts USBaudio for the first active client, and stops it when the last active device-client stops. Add/Remove callbacks discard client metadata; Will/Begin/Do callbacks ignore the client argument while offering ReadInput and WriteMix.
findings.consequence: This implements aggregate device lifetime. Ignoring unused clientmetadata or offering the same operations to clients is not by itself a proved SDK violation.

findings.claim: IOProcStreamUsage is absent from the native plug-in supported property selectors; native get/set paths reject unsupported selectors.
findings.consequence: Successful public IOProc mask queries are not evidence that these masks entered this native handler. An intervening host/client layer answering them is a source-level inference; which internal component dispatched the observed buffer is unproved.

findings.claim: Global output IsActive is a separate native Boolean. Its setter updates USB desired output activity and currentISO state; republishing an audio engine reapplies desired activity. The ISO clear function conditionally invokes the original ring-clear routine when inactive, PCMready, render lock available and either output_written or output_ring.stream_written is set. Service invokes the clear helper. Inactive render skips new ring writes.
findings.consequence: The existing NI-derived clear path is present. output_written can be set before a priming no-op or render-lock/write outcome, so the flag alone is not proof that PCM was written. Source presence and call edges do not establish physical last-output behavior or exact runtime cadence.

findings.claim: No admitted contract equates one IOProc output mask zero with global output-stream IsActive zero or last device-client StopIO. The native source has no explicit mapping from those public per-IOProc masks into its global activity Boolean.
findings.consequence: Per-IOProc routing qualification, aggregate device Start/Stop, and global output-inactive ring clearing are separate obligations. The last-output test has not established that it exercised the native global inactive boundary.

decision.why: No causal evidence justifies an ARM binding repair from retained public masks alone. The helper uses returned IDs consistently with SDK; the global output-clear path already exists. Preserve original NI timing/ring/recovery and the strict unused-buffer assertion.
decision.minimum_remaining_question: What host-origin client and global stream-activity events occur while one output consumer stops and an input consumer stays active?
decision.next_step_before_code: Record one bounded host-boundary event observation plan in existingM3 covering device-client Start/Stop and global output IsActive transitions; keep it separate from the unresolved public IOProc NULL-buffer assertion. No probe or temporary instrumentation is implemented/admitted by this read-only audit.
decision.limits: Do not swap registration IDs for raw callback pointers, add a native IOProcStreamUsage selector, change scheduling, force global activity to claim natural client-stop success, or declare parity from this source audit.
